steps.text: Part 2 of 3: Development: a lead you can spend. This part covers Build it, or stop it; Near misses and a mixed test. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

**Build a lead.** Make each move do a job. Develop with a threat, so the opponent must answer instead of developing. Castle early. Early queen moves usually lose time unless each carries a threat. **Defend against one.** Develop a defender, trade the attacker, give the king a square. [I] Closing the centre may help, but the test position below is a case where capturing is best. Capablanca and Emanuel Lasker both urged bringing the pieces out quickly; see the sources.

steps.title: The Légal trap and its near misses
steps.prompt: Original first: Black has pinned with ...Bg4 and kept the pin with ...Bh5. Then his knight is on f6. Then he has played ...a6. Predict whether Nxe5 works each time.
steps.chapter: Near misses and a mixed test

steps.caption: Black to move. White threatens mate in one. Black wins time by answering with a developing threat.

line.say: The pawn attacks the queen. White must spend another move on her.
The queen retreats and still eyes f7.
The knight develops and blocks the f-file. Black has two pieces out; White has a bishop and a queen that moved twice.

claims.statement: If Black passes, Qxf7 is checkmate.
At depth 16 g6 and Qe7 are the engine's best moves, within 40 centipawns.

steps.caption: The other side of the coin: White has given a pawn (two, until White wins one back). Count: White has a knight, a bishop and castling, Black a knight and a bishop. At depth 16 the engine rates the start as level. [H] At club level the lead may count for more.

line.say: Black develops a piece and keeps his extra material for now.
White takes one pawn back and has pawns on d4 and e4.
Black fights for the centre and opens lines for his bishop.
White takes, and the e-file is open while Black's king is still on e8.
Black recaptures. White's king is castled; Black's is not.

claims.statement: The engine rates the starting position within 0.45 pawns of level.
Nf6 and Nge7 are Black's best moves, within 40 centipawns.
After exd5 the e-file is the only open file.
Black's king is still on e8.

steps.text: Nimzowitsch warned against pawn-grabbing while development is unfinished: "Never play to win a pawn while your development is yet unfinished!" (*My System*). He allowed one exception, a centre pawn taken without much danger. A gambit is the same trade seen from the other side: Emanuel Lasker described it as a pawn given for time and open lines. [I] The price is paid in tempi.

steps.title: King still in the centre
steps.prompt: Original first: the e-pawn is on e4. Then it is on e3. Is castling equally urgent? Predict.

steps.caption: Black to move, one move before the first board. Two defences work (develop the king's knight, or open the bishop's diagonal with e6; depth 16). The pawn push of the first board gives White a sacrifice worth over three pawns. Defend by developing a defender or blocking the diagonal, not by chasing the bishop with a pawn.

line.say: Black develops a piece first. The king now has g8 if the bishop ever lands on f7.
White asks the bishop on g4 what it wants.
Black trades the bishop for the knight and removes a White attacker.
The queen recaptures.
Black opens the f8 bishop and covers d5 and f5.
White takes space in the centre.

claims.statement: The pawn push ...b5 is at least two pawns worse than the best moves.
Nf6 and e6 are the engine's best moves, within 40 centipawns.

steps.caption: Why ...Nf6 spoils it: a developed piece guards the bishop.

line.say: The same knight capture.
Black takes the knight.
The queen takes the bishop...
...and the knight on f6 takes the queen. The extra defender ruins the idea.

claims.statement: At depth 16 Nxe5 is at least five pawns worse than the best move.
The knight on f6 defends h5.

steps.caption: Why castling comes first here: the centre can open at once.

line.say: The king leaves the e-file and the rook goes to f1.
Black opens the centre.
White recaptures, and the e-file is open with White's king already safe.
Black attacks the bishop.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is O-O.
Moving the king to f1 is at least a pawn worse.
Qe2 is at least 0.8 pawns worse.

steps.caption: Same position, same plan, but White plays the queen move instead of castling. The opened e-file now runs toward White's own king, with the queen and the bishop stuck on it. With castling the file was White's; here the engine's edge shrinks from about +2.0 to about +0.2 (depth 16).

line.say: The queen leaves the king on e1 without a safe square.
Black opens the centre.
White recaptures; the bishop now stands on the e-file in front of the queen.
The knight attacks the bishop, which is tied to the queen behind it.

claims.statement: White's king is still on e1.
Qe2 is at least 0.8 pawns worse than the best move.
